title: Fault injection: every injected fault leaves the last valid record, a damaged newest record is rolled back by name, and the resume reproduces the uninterrupted run

fixture.scene: tests/test_differentiable.py::project(steps=13): 2D 16 x 15 cells, mesh 0.1 um, three-cell PML with a four-layer CPML on x_min, one continuous point source, three point monitors, float64, epsilon 1.7
fixture.policy: slab width 4, temporal depth 3 (five blocks, the last partial), checkpoints 1, local checkpoints 1, restart_every_blocks 1 (2 in one cancellation instance), host or file-backed banks, CPU or CUDA tiles
faults: forward interruption after two blocks (host and disk banks)
backward interruption after two transposes (CPU host, CUDA disk)
process kill of a child process during forward and during backward (subprocess, disk banks)
ENOSPC raised by the write of state-0.bin, meta.json, latest-forward.json of the second forward record and gradient.bin of the second backward record
torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError raised inside the 25th slab update (first update of the third block, CUDA)
EIO raised by the next file-bank read (index_select) and write (index_copy_) once the journal holds backward-3

state-0.bin truncated to half and one byte of signals.bin flipped in the newest forward record; adjoint-1.bin flipped, gradient.bin truncated in the newest backward record with a fallback, gradient.bin flipped in a first backward record without a fallback; a checksum removed from meta.json; meta.json unreadable with a truncated fallback
RuntimeError raised by the next host-to-device (_copy_into) and device-to-host (to_host) tile transfer once the journal holds backward-3 (CUDA)
cancel event set during the third forward block (every 1 and every 2) and during the third transpose

reference_method: behavioural: the same scene run uninterrupted without a journal in the same process; after the fault, the pointer names the last record published before it, the journal's status names the fault, and a second run resumes from that record

observables.name: surviving_record
observables.definition: block named by latest-<kind>.json after the fault, and the fallback it names

observables.name: rollback
observables.definition: entries of report['restart_rollbacks'] for a damaged newest record

observables.name: terminal_state
observables.definition: status.json state after the fault (failed or cancelled) and after the resume (completed), with the failure reason text

observables.name: resume_agreement
observables.definition: difference between the resumed and the uninterrupted signals and gradient

observables.name: leaks
observables.definition: entries under the scratch directory and torch.cuda.memory_allocated after the faulty run and after the resume, against the values before the faulty run

acceptance.last_valid_record: after every fault the pointer of the interrupted kind names a record published before the fault and that record passes the integrity checks; for a fault while writing record N, the pointer names N-1 (block 1 for the forward faults, block 4 for the backward faults)
acceptance.damaged_newest_record: a truncated, corrupted or checksum-less newest record is rolled back to its fallback (the previous record of that kind) or, without one, to the empty journal of that kind; report['restart_rollbacks'] names the record, the reason (file and check) and the fallback
acceptance.terminal_state: an exception leaves status.json as failed with the exception type and message; a cancel event leaves it cancelled with the phase and block; the resume ends with completed
acceptance.resume: the resumed signals and gradient agree with the uninterrupted run within rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-6 on CPU and CUDA (proposed_thresholds discrete_dimensionless_fp32), and bitwise on CPU
acceptance.no_leaks: the scratch directory is empty after the faulty run and after the resume (the killed process's own bank excepted and removed by the test), and torch.cuda.memory_allocated returns to the value measured before the faulty run
acceptance.source_of_limits: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds discrete_dimensionless_fp32; file and byte counts are exact

not_yet_covered: faults inside the dispersive (ADE), tensor, geometry and modal streamed paths
a real out-of-space volume (ENOSPC is raised by a monkeypatched write)

applicability: Streamed X-slab runs with a durable journal on one workstation; the injected faults are raised by monkeypatched methods or a killed child process, not by real hardware faults.
notes: Declared after the journal gained checksummed records, one fallback record per kind, ownership and terminal states on branch g5-restart; the limits are the program's fp32 pair and exact counts, no fixture-specific budget.
